title: Last Week in AI Agents
description: A weekly breakdown of all things AI assistants & agentic economy
author: David Pawlan
html:
Welcome to your weekly breakdown of all things AI Assistant and the agentic economy.

If you know someone who you think would find this valuable, please forward their way so they can subscribe! - David

What’s Trending?

Uber, Airbnb, and DoorDash report shockingly low agent-driven orders

Uber said AI agents booked just four rides during Halloween week, while Airbnb called bookings from Muse and Instinct “very non-material”. That follows DoorDash’s earlier disclosure that third-party agents had placed only several hundred orders in total. These claims highlight the difficulty in reporting agent-driven behavior.

Apple opens Siri AI to developers

Apple opened a developer preview that lets apps connect their content and actions to Siri AI, including skills that chain multiple actions together. Siri can use personal context and what’s on your screen to understand requests, then act across participating apps.

Amazon opens text-to-shop with Alexa

Amazon is rolling out shopping over text with Alexa, letting customers search for products, add them to their cart, and buy without opening the app. The launch comes after Amazon blocked Muse from accessing its site in September.

AI Assistant Competition Updates

  • Muse launched Voice, introduced Spaces for custom planners, trackers, and games, upgraded its models with Active Memory and Active Focus, and expanded to Mexico.

  • Grok Bot launched a shopping experience for comparing deals and tracking orders and added phone calls.

  • Siri opened a developer preview for apps to integrate their content and actions and added Siri Recap and Live Rewind in the watchOS 27.3 beta.

  • Alexa launched text-to-shop, letting customers search, compare, and buy through text messages.

  • Quest launched a personal agent with its own Android phone, custom iOS mini-apps, and the ability to manage Instinct and Muse.

  • Tomo added Shop Pay checkout through Shopify Catalog in iMessage and released Dachi 1.0, its first in-house model tuned for everyday conversation and agent tasks.

  • Pally added Zapier and custom MCP servers, turned its morning brief into an actionable page with one-tap approvals, launched in Slack, and added support for 22 languages.

  • Fo partnered with Twilio to power phone calls and launched Fo Friends so users’ agents can coordinate with each other.

  • Keiki added Apple Messages for Business in early access and launched agent-to-agent support so other agents can find and message Keiki agents.

  • Town added recruiting shortlists and call prep through Greenhouse, Ashby, and Stardex, shipped Townie status indicators, and launched a Mercury integration.

  • Wabi launched on Windows and added Shopify shopping and Shop Pay checkout in group chats.

The Agentic Economy

Cloudflare:

Cloudflare added a Personal Assistants category so websites can see which agents visit and set access controls for each one.

This is the next step in agent-tracking.

Musk:

Grok Bot adds stricter limits after Musk claims that their costs are unsustainably high.

Aina:

Preorders opened for a ring with a screen that predicts your next three actions and lets you approve agent tasks with a thumb flick.

Jinko:

A travel search and booking API built for agents is here, giving assistants infra for completing travel transactions.

Mastercard:

The company disclosed partnerships with OpenAI and Tencent to advance the payment infra of agentic commerce.

Agents in the Wild! An Agent…

  • searched old iMessages to find a buddy’s apartment number

  • caught a coffee-shop overcharge and helped recover $200, plus a coffee and croissant.

  • helped land a paid internship in New Zealand, handling applications, interviews, and flight booking.

  • reordered CPAP supplies through the VA, waiting on hold and requesting the exact mask needed.

  • cancelled an unwanted Discord subscription and secured a refund in 15 minutes.

  • caught an Airbnb host’s deadline that another assistant missed.

  • coordinated with another agent to check calendars and book a meeting.

  • turned cold sales emails into sponsorship leads and tracked bookings and campaign dates.

  • organized classes, deadlines, and exams, then booked flights to a sister’s wedding.

  • negotiated an internet bill, saving $40 a month.

  • monitored a YouTube playlist and turned new videos into transcripts, analysis, and briefings.

Prompt of the Week

On Deck

Publishing on the Agentic Web
November 9 · NYC

Betaworks hosts a discussion on publisher traffic, attribution, and revenue when agents read the web.

The question is how publishers get paid and credited when an assistant delivers the answer instead of sending a visitor. Free; approval required.

RSVP here.

Interchange: A Private Dinner for Agentic Commerce Builders
November 12 · San Francisco

Coinflow brings together builders working on agents that book, buy, and pay.

The dinner focuses on what changes when software becomes the customer acting on someone’s behalf. Free; approval required.

RSVP here.

Your Agent, Every Inbox
November 12 · NYC

Monad Foundation’s Studio AI Lab explores agents and inboxes.

It’s relevant to anyone thinking about how assistants can turn everyday messages into useful actions.

RSVP here.

title: Nov 2nd: The Past Week in AI Agents
description: A weekly breakdown of all things AI assistants & agentic economy
author: David Pawlan
html:
Happy Monday!

Welcome to your weekly breakdown of all things AI Assistant and the agentic economy.

If you know someone who you think would find this valuable, please forward their way so they can subscribe!

All the best,
David

What’s Trending?

Wabi raised $55M at a $1.25B valuation

Wabi, the multiplayer agent that builds mini-apps you share with friends, raised $55M at a $1.25B valuation. IVP led the round, with a16z, Forerunner, the Alexa Fund, Tobi Lütke and Marc Benioff joining.

It's the first multiplayer agent app valued at more than $1B.

Two new agents come out of stealth

Rocker came out of stealth with $12.85M for an enterprise AI assistant. It runs in the customer's cloud and catches the "oh shit" moments managers would otherwise miss.

Robyn launched invite-only as a "personal agentic platform" that spins up a fleet of agents that already know your context from a single sentence.

Anthropic filed it’s S-1 to go public

Anthropic filed an S-1 with the SEC for an IPO and plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The filing covers Class A common stock, and it means Anthropic's finances will become public for the first time.

The number of shares and the price range haven't been set yet.

AI Assistant Competition Updates

  • Instinct is reportedly raising at a $30B valuation. They’ve also added an Action Button shortcut, Link balance, opened group chats to everyone, added Shop Pay at any store, partnered with OpenTable, and expanded its 1Password partnership.

  • Ollie announced it's shutting down Nov 6, saying it couldn't keep up once Muse, Instinct and others entered the space.

  • ChatGPT added iCloud Mail and Calendar which lends it to operate like an AI agent

  • Pally launched city lookup to find everyone you know, Inbox Triage, Money Back and Bills & Renewals, and added shopping at 23 stores.

  • Tomo launched Community recommendations and Selective Context for group chats.

  • Fo launched Fompt Feed and is live on Slack and email cc.

  • Muse launched in Singapore and added the iOS Share sheet.

  • Grok Bot shipped Vault, 1Password and Apple app integrations and showed shared bots its sales team built.

The Agentic Economy

McKinsey:

McKinsey surveyed about 21,000 consumers across 11 markets and found more than half now use AI to shop. In the US, the rate of AI users finishing a purchase with AI jumped 70% from last year. For people using AI, AI search is three times as influential as regular search, and stand-alone AI tools beat retailers' own assistants until checkout.

Ken Huang:

No single agentic commerce standard is going to win. Instead, the stack is splitting into layers: Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, Google and x402 handle checkout and settlement, while MCP and the Agent Name Service handle context and discovery. The buyer's agent becomes its own payment actor, holding the credential while the card networks hold the risk.

Browserbase:

Browserbase launched BELL, an open-source kit for building your own personal assistant. Browserbase for the browser, eve by Vercel for the agent, Linq for iMessage and Link by Stripe for payments.

Agents in the Wild! An Agent…

  • switched a GEICO policy to Progressive, saving $1,174 a year.

  • found and hired a person for a day of promo work at $149.

  • caught two years of double billing and got $834 back from Terminix.

  • cleared a busy office room by offering people other rooms.

  • negotiated an internet bill down from $99.99 to $54.99.

  • is logging spam texts as possible legal violations worth $500 to $1,500 each.

  • noticed non-English IMAX tickets and got a refund, avoided the wrong language.

  • read phone and internet bills and saved about €469 a year.

Prompt of the Week

On Deck

Hello World by Linq

Hello World is on Nov 3 and brings together founders, engineers and investors who are building agentic products and infrastructure. The speakers come from Skye, OpenAI, Town, Stripe, DoorDash, Lindy, Browserbase and a16z.

That's a good spread of the companies in this newsletter, from assistants to payments to the browser infrastructure agents run on.

title: October 26th: Last Week in AI Agents
description: A weekly breakdown of all things AI assistants & agentic economy
author: David Pawlan
html:
Happy Monday!

Welcome to your weekly breakdown of all things AI Assistant and the agentic economy.

If you know someone who you think would find this valuable, please forward their way so they can subscribe!

All the best,
David

What’s Trending?

Anthropic launched Claude Duet

Anthropic has joined the race by launching a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent. It comes to you with what needs your attention, does the tasks you hand it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts for you.

Access and pricing for the preview aren’t public yet.

Walmart opened its store to AI agents

Walmart launched Agent Gateway, an MCP connection that lets approved agents search Walmart and Sam’s Club and buy for you without seeing your personal info or purchase history. Next month, each agent gets its own Agent Profile in your account, with purchases shown separately and either per-order approval or a spending cap you set.

1Password launches for Agents

1Password announced 1Password for Agents, letting agents sign into sites for you without ever needing your password. No more re-uploading passwords for each agent.

Launch partners include Muse, Grok Bot, Claude, OpenAI, Town, Instinct, Tomo, Perplexity and more.

AI Assistant Competition Updates

  • Grok Bot had a big week: Pages for reports, memos and dashboards; phone access to Calendar, Reminders, Contacts and more on iOS and Android; and 0.77 prerelease builds that most notably add the ability to make Calls (dial, hold, press keys, live transcript).

  • Wabi launched 2.0, a group agent that lives in one shared thread with your partner, friends or family and handles calendars, tickets and trips.

  • Town raised a $108M Series B at a $1B valuation for multiplayer work assistants (“Townies”) that ask each other questions and share only what their person would.

  • Wajo launched Fo MCP, which lets the assistant control physical devices, from a lamp that gives reminders to a vacuum that deep-cleans.

  • humans& introduced Boba, a social AI you can text or message at boba.app (details beyond the tagline are still thin).

  • Muse crossed 10M+ users in about 40 days, with shopping among the top activities.

The Agentic Economy

Yelp:

Yelp launched Check for Me, an AI phone agent that calls a restaurant for you, asks about the wait, and texts you back. OpenTable booking inside Yelp Assistant is rolling out too.

Mastercard:

Mastercard opened early access to Agent Pay for Machines after pilots with Coinbase, Base, Cloudflare and others. Agents get APIs and a sandbox to make machine payments, including via x402.

Gigi:

Clara Gold launched Gigi, an agentic network that helps your agent find warm intros. Your agent searches your network, then asks the agents of people you trust to search theirs, without exposing contacts or reading anyone’s email.

phoneuse:

Abdulla Ababakre launched phoneuse, an MCP/API that gives AI agents their own cloud phones, real Androids and real iPhones. You tell the agent what to do, and it taps through apps the way a person would, which matters for services that only really work on a phone.

Agents in the Wild! An Agent…

  • Flagged a $70 Amazon restocking fee on a car-seat return and got the credit with a call script.

  • Found a $1k cheaper direct flight on a nicer airline after the booking was already made.

  • Chased a mistaken $350/mo plan until it was cancelled with months refunded.

  • Cut ~$850/yr off a phone bill, killed ~$1,178/yr in subscriptions, and got ~$1,245 refunded.

  • Took over a 2-year Google Fi claim and calculated the refund.

  • Ordered an Ollyball from one text; the package arrived without opening a website.

  • Got a free Starlink replacement kit by running the support chat.

  • Filed a homestead exemption worth ~$4K and switched car insurance for ~$1.5K/yr.

  • Cancelled 5 subscriptions (~$872/yr) and paused lawn care.

  • Finds Hawaii dates, builds the itinerary, and books flights after months of stalled planning.

  • Proactively offered to reorder groceries, asked once, then placed the order.

Prompt of the Week

On Deck

iMessage Agent Founder Pitch by Photon

We’re bringing 5 to 10 of the best personal agent founders to Corgi Cafe for one night of pitches. Each founder gets the floor to show what their agent does that nobody else’s can, and walk through how they got their first 500 users.

Wednesday, October 28th: Event Link

title: October 19th: AI Assistants & The Agentic Economy
description: A weekly breakdown of all things AI assistants & agentic economy
author: David Pawlan
html:
Happy Monday!

Welcome to the second edition of At Your Service, the weekly breakdown of all things AI Assistant and the agentic economy.

If you know someone who you think would find this valuable, please forward their way so they can subscribe!

All the best,
David

What’s Trending?

Meta launched Muse Wonder

Meta announced Muse Wonder, a new family of frontier models built for personal and professional agent work. Alexandr Wang says it adds "active memory," so Muse can remember what you told it days or weeks ago and use that on future tasks.

On Cheeky Pint with John Collison, Wang said Muse is "one of the first products where people are fully delegating purchases to the agents." Zuck added that "every business is going to have agents too."

AI Assistants Rank on 14-Day Retention

Muse's D14 retention numbers last week were shared, and they're close to ChatGPT's, sitting at 22.5% compared to ChatGPT’s 26.8%.

I personally messaged dozens of iMessage based AI-assistant founders to get a better grasp of what the general industry D14 stats are looking like. Self-reported numbers ranged from ~20% to a handful that independently reported sitting between 40-50%.

One remaining question: what defines retention rates for iMessage-based apps?

AI Assistant Consumer Travel Report

This report tested five AI assistants on booking travel: Instinct, Muse, GrokBot, Dots and Miso. Each was scored on eight areas, from booking time and seat selection to cancellation and rebooking.

All five booked a flight, but only some could change one afterward. Miso won the battle, with Instinct coming in at a close second.

Grok Bot, Dots & Muse struggled in their own ways while being painfully slow.

AI Assistant Competition Updates

  • Amazon launched Bee, a hardware first AI-assistant that leans into the ambient assistant experience.

  • Hark added Action Buttons to help you cleanly kick off tasks based on what it knows from you.

  • Hark gave away $1 million of free pizza across the US, ordered by its agent. A bug charged some users full price and users complained about privacy policies.

  • GrokBot added new connectors to Robinhood, Coinbase, Trello, PostHog, beehiiv, eToro, and more.

  • Pally now let’s you manage your X DMs straight from iMessage.

  • Caddy built a full interface within the iMessage experience.

  • Manus added scheduled automations, letting you put tasks on autopilot.

The Agentic Economy

Elon Musk:

He hit back at Amazon after reports that it's blocking Grok's shopping agents. He floated the idea of building a company to compete against Amazon in this world of agentic commerce.

Shopify's Tobi Lütke:

He introduced shop.md, a plain file that tells AI agents what a store sells and how they can buy from it.

JPMorgan (via CNBC):

America's biggest bank has officially blocked companies like Instinct and Muse from accessing Chase accounts via browser-use.

“We’re not going to allow [it]…it’s just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan.”

Google:

Google launched Universal Cart in Search and the Gemini app, letting people check out across many stores in one cart, which is the same kind of buying an agent would do for you.

Agents in the Wild

  • Notion's Akshay Kothari built a "context vault" in Notion that every agent he uses reads from and writes new memories back to.

  • An agent tracked down a sold-out iPhone 18 Pro Max by emailing stores until it found one

  • An agent got a user $500 back for a delayed flight

  • One user used an Assistant to track her son’s flight to surprise him and pick him up at the airport.

  • An agent saved a user over $1,300 after finding numerous unused subscriptions.

Prompt of the Week

On Deck

SF AI Assistant Meetup: October 19th

If you are in SF, come by our AI assistant meetup tonight! We’ll have 10 different AI assistant companies presenting, with some fun surprises to be announced at the event.

You won’t want to miss it!

title: Welcome to the first AI Assistant Newsletter
description: A weekly breakdown of all things AI assistants & agentic economy
author: David Pawlan
html:
Happy Monday!

The AI assistant race is on, and it seems like there is a breaking news story every single day. As I’ve been testing every single AI assistant myself, and am now chronically online keeping track of all the updates, it only made sense to start a newsletter to help others stay on top of all that is happening.

That is what I’m here for, at your service, to keep you locked in on what you need to know. This is my first one, so if there is any feedback on how I can make this newsletter more helpful, please let me know!

All the best,
David

What’s Trending?

Personal Agent Protocol (PAP)

Sierra and Meta announced a standard for personal assistants to interact with businesses through websites, APIs and business agents. Partners include Shopify, Stripe and Walmart. First specification expected later in October.

Separately, Decagon open-sourced a consent-and-trust protocol, co-developed with Instinct using A2A and OAuth, and joined the PAP working group.

AI Assistants Join Group Chats

Three different assistants made moves into group chats this week.

  1. Instinct is rolling out early access to an assistant that helps your group plan trips, find tickets and coordinate schedules.

  2. Pally launches group chats.

  3. Tomo brings people with shared goals together in assistant-facilitated chats.

  4. Fo is expanding into Telegram group chats.

a16z’s Top 100 Consumer AI Apps report

This report, authored by Olivia Moore, analyzes the top 100 consumer AI apps, examining adoption, usage trends, monetization, and emerging categories.

It includes a section on what people using AI assistants are actually talking about. The data was pulled from the 1,500+ people in the AI assistant group chats I have personally put together.

Top topics: coding, travel, & shopping

AI Assistant Competition Updates

  • Instinct announced Instinct Concierge, native customer service, as well as their new hotel booking experience.

  • GrokBot launched its own email that your bot can use on your behalf for things like signups or bookings.

  • Pally slashes their pricing, making their entire app free.

  • Natura announced the release of a ring, bringing their AI assistant to hardware.

  • Hark founder announced 280K+ users with 4.3M messages sent within 48 hours of their launch.

The Agentic Economy

Stripe’s Patrick Collison:

Personal agents could make buyers more rational and weaken businesses’ ability to profit from inattention, coupons, price discrimination and insurance upsells.

Meta’s Alexandr Wang:

One month after launch, he highlights the AI assistant wins like people using Muse to save time and money.

Paul Graham:

Amazon’s restrictions on AI agents creates an opening for a competitor.

Agents in the Wild

  • Muse cancels insurance and reportedly saves $700+

  • An agent runs home automations like controlling the blinds and AC

  • A user says Hark discovered a forgotten refund email and received an $800 refund

  • An agent designed and 3D-printed a replacement glue-stick cap

  • Muse finds a similar standing desk for $300 less

  • Someone used Instinct to help find a new dog to adopt that looked like their old dog

Prompt of the Week

On Deck

SF AI Assistant Meetup: October 19th

If you are in SF, come by our AI assistant meetup! I’m excited to bring together lovers of AI assistants. You will also get the chance to hear from countless AI assistant companies as they pitch why their product is better than the rest!
